Source_Document: 2024 Solo Female Travel Trends and Statistics.html
Document_Title: 2024 Solo Female Travel Trends and Statistics
Verbatim_Quote: 1. Solo female travel is a travel style, not a lifestyle: Only 23% of respondents are exclusive solo travelers, the majority also traveled with others in the last 12 months.

Segment_ID: 2024 Solo Female Travel Trends and Statistics.html_P031
Source_Document: 2024 Solo Female Travel Trends and Statistics.html
Document_Title: 2024 Solo Female Travel Trends and Statistics
Verbatim_Quote: 2. Interest in group travel is strong: 14% plan to travel on a women-only trip in 2025, 22% on a mixed-gender group trip. These figures have increased from 2022, 2023 and 2024.

Segment_ID: 2024 Solo Female Travel Trends and Statistics.html_P032
Source_Document: 2024 Solo Female Travel Trends and Statistics.html
Document_Title: 2024 Solo Female Travel Trends and Statistics
Verbatim_Quote: 3. Women travel solo because they want to: The main reasons women travel solo are: 1) Freedom and flexibility (87% ), 2) Escape from routine and responsibilities (83% ), 3) Relax, self-care and enjoy me-time (79% ), 4) Challenge themselves (74% ). This ranking holds for all age groups and has remained stable since 2020. 55% of women travel solo because they have nobody to go with.

Segment_ID: 2024 Solo Female Travel Trends and Statistics.html_P033
Source_Document: 2024 Solo Female Travel Trends and Statistics.html
Document_Title: 2024 Solo Female Travel Trends and Statistics
Verbatim_Quote: 4. Women worry a lot when traveling solo: 1) Personal safety (66% ), 2) Higher costs vs splitting costs with a travel companion (66% ), 3) Something bad happening (37% ), 4) Language barriers (42% ), 5) Getting lost or feeling lonely (35% and 33% ). 20% worry about dining alone.

Segment_ID: 2024 Solo Female Travel Trends and Statistics.html_P034
Source_Document: 2024 Solo Female Travel Trends and Statistics.html
Document_Title: 2024 Solo Female Travel Trends and Statistics
Verbatim_Quote: 5. Barriers to starting solo traveling: Those who have never traveled on their own worry about safety (59% ) and about higher costs (71% ). 44% do not travel solo because they wouldn’t have someone to share the experience with. 15% would feel guilty leaving loved ones behind and 11% don’t travel solo because their husband or family are against it. 11% didn’t know solo travel was an option for them. 75% would be more likely to book a solo trip if joining a women-only tour.

Segment_ID: 2024 Solo Female Travel Trends and Statistics.html_P035
Source_Document: 2024 Solo Female Travel Trends and Statistics.html
Document_Title: 2024 Solo Female Travel Trends and Statistics
Verbatim_Quote: 6. Experience helps feel safer: Safety worries decrease from 77% to 55% for those with more than 10 solo trips vis-a-vis those who have taken less than 5. Even though experience helps, safety remains a universal and unanimous concern for solo female travelers.

Segment_ID: 2024 Solo Female Travel Trends and Statistics.html_P036
Source_Document: 2024 Solo Female Travel Trends and Statistics.html
Document_Title: 2024 Solo Female Travel Trends and Statistics
Verbatim_Quote: 7. Safety concerns are warranted: 21% of solo female travelers have feared for their safety in the last 12 months during a solo trip. 1% of the respondents did not manage to keep themselves safe.

Segment_ID: 2024 Solo Female Travel Trends and Statistics.html_P037
Source_Document: 2024 Solo Female Travel Trends and Statistics.html
Document_Title: 2024 Solo Female Travel Trends and Statistics
Verbatim_Quote: 8. Women protect themselves with safety devices: 17% of respondents carried self-defense items when they traveled in 2024, from guns (predominantly US domestic travel) and knives to key rings, pepper spray, alarms or whistles. Airtags are increasingly used as safety devices and a means for their loved ones to track them. 37% used anti-theft bags on their trips. The older the traveler, the higher their likelihood of using one (Boomers 53% vs. Gen Z 25% ).

Segment_ID: 2024 Solo Female Travel Trends and Statistics.html_P038
Source_Document: 2024 Solo Female Travel Trends and Statistics.html
Document_Title: 2024 Solo Female Travel Trends and Statistics
Verbatim_Quote: 9. Insurance: On their solo trips in 2023, 55% of respondents always bought travel insurance and 47% always bought medical insurance.

Segment_ID: 2024 Solo Female Travel Trends and Statistics.html_P039
Source_Document: 2024 Solo Female Travel Trends and Statistics.html
Document_Title: 2024 Solo Female Travel Trends and Statistics
Verbatim_Quote: 10. Your own country is your best first solo trip: 16% of respondents recommend one’s own country for a first solo trip.

Segment_ID: 2024 Solo Female Travel Trends and Statistics.html_P040
Source_Document: 2024 Solo Female Travel Trends and Statistics.html
Document_Title: 2024 Solo Female Travel Trends and Statistics
Verbatim_Quote: 11. Europe remains the Best international destination for a first solo trip: European countries (54% ) are the best destination for a first solo trip. The top countries are UK, Italy, Thailand, Spain, Japan. These are the same countries mentioned in the previous years but Japan replacing Portugal.

Segment_ID: 2024 Solo Female Travel Trends and Statistics.html_P041
Source_Document: 2024 Solo Female Travel Trends and Statistics.html
Document_Title: 2024 Solo Female Travel Trends and Statistics
Verbatim_Quote: 12. Women traveling solo trust recommendations likeminded women & loved ones: Advice from solo female travel Facebook groups (81% ) is the most trusted, more than recommendations from friends and family (72% ) who may not have experience traveling solo, Online review sites (64% ), and Travel blogs (62% ).

Segment_ID: 2024 Solo Female Travel Trends and Statistics.html_P042
Source_Document: 2024 Solo Female Travel Trends and Statistics.html
Document_Title: 2024 Solo Female Travel Trends and Statistics
Verbatim_Quote: 13. Least trustworthy recommendations come from: TV (48% ) and Online ads (47%), Influencers (31% ), Online and print magazines (19% ). Government travel advisories went from not trusted in previous years (hello pandemic) to trusted by 56% in 2025.

Segment_ID: 2024 Solo Female Travel Trends and Statistics.html_P043
Source_Document: 2024 Solo Female Travel Trends and Statistics.html
Document_Title: 2024 Solo Female Travel Trends and Statistics
Verbatim_Quote: 14. Bucket list destinations: The most desired solo destinations are Japan, Australia, Iceland, Italy, Greece, and New Zealand.

Segment_ID: 2024 Solo Female Travel Trends and Statistics.html_P044
Source_Document: 2024 Solo Female Travel Trends and Statistics.html
Document_Title: 2024 Solo Female Travel Trends and Statistics
Verbatim_Quote: 15. Favorite city for a solo trip: London, Paris, Rome, Barcelona & Tokyo top the list for a solo trip thanks to the cultural offers, the many things to do, relative safety and ease of getting around. New York drops from the top of the list (vs 2024), Tokyo gets added.

Segment_ID: 2024 Solo Female Travel Trends and Statistics.html_P045
Source_Document: 2024 Solo Female Travel Trends and Statistics.html
Document_Title: 2024 Solo Female Travel Trends and Statistics
Verbatim_Quote: 16. Women choose destinations based on its overall appeal: Cultural attractions (77% ), Beauty of a destination (69% ), the Local cuisine (65% ), Safety of the destination (62% ), Access to nature (59% ), Good weather (57% ), Friendliness of the locals (54% ), Value for money (53% ) and the Country’s reputation (50% ) are top decision factors.

Segment_ID: 2024 Solo Female Travel Trends and Statistics.html_P046
Source_Document: 2024 Solo Female Travel Trends and Statistics.html
Document_Title: 2024 Solo Female Travel Trends and Statistics
Verbatim_Quote: 17. Unimportant aspects when choosing a destination: Closeness to home (2%), Opportunities for Instagram shots (9% ), the way the destination handled COVID (8% ) or good shopping opportunities (12% ), are not important in 2025.

Segment_ID: 2024 Solo Female Travel Trends and Statistics.html_P047
Source_Document: 2024 Solo Female Travel Trends and Statistics.html
Document_Title: 2024 Solo Female Travel Trends and Statistics
Verbatim_Quote: 18. The local connection is important: 65% actively tried to meet locals during their solo trips, 59% of solo female travelers used the services of a guide at least once.

Segment_ID: 2024 Solo Female Travel Trends and Statistics.html_P048
Source_Document: 2024 Solo Female Travel Trends and Statistics.html
Document_Title: 2024 Solo Female Travel Trends and Statistics
Verbatim_Quote: 20. Purchase decision factors: Price drives the decisions of 56% of women when choosing a travel provider. Beyond price, 33% of women traveling solo care about a travel provider’s eco-friendliness and care for the environment, 29% care about whether a business is locally owned, and 22% values its social responsibility. 15% of women value female-owned businesses.

Document_Title: 25+ Solo Travel Safety Tips for Women
Verbatim_Quote: “Is it safe to travel solo?” is one of the top questions I get when traveling alone. So it is critical to know solo travel safety tips to ease that anxiety and fear. I mean, hopping on a flight to another country abroad takes guts, but we still need to take precautions.

Segment_ID: 25+ Solo Travel Safety Tips for Women _ Sojournies.html_P002
Source_Document: 25+ Solo Travel Safety Tips for Women _ Sojournies.html
Document_Title: 25+ Solo Travel Safety Tips for Women
Verbatim_Quote: There is nothing like that first solo trip. The mix of anxiousness and adrenaline makes it such an adventurous experience. And while there are many advantages and disadvantages to solo travel, and what we need to feel secure is relative, here are safety tips for traveling alone.

Segment_ID: 25+ Solo Travel Safety Tips for Women _ Sojournies.html_P003
Source_Document: 25+ Solo Travel Safety Tips for Women _ Sojournies.html
Document_Title: 25+ Solo Travel Safety Tips for Women

Lucky for you, it doesn’t change the price for you at all, and it’s a super easy and generous way to say thanks for all the work I put into writing this post!!)

Segment_ID: 25+ Solo Travel Safety Tips for Women _ Sojournies.html_P004
Source_Document: 25+ Solo Travel Safety Tips for Women _ Sojournies.html
Document_Title: 25+ Solo Travel Safety Tips for Women
Verbatim_Quote: There are many reasons why people travel solo. Some can find other people to travel with because it is difficult to align your schedule with your friends. Other people enjoy their time alone and don’t want to be bothered.

Segment_ID: 25+ Solo Travel Safety Tips for Women _ Sojournies.html_P005
Source_Document: 25+ Solo Travel Safety Tips for Women _ Sojournies.html
Document_Title: 25+ Solo Travel Safety Tips for Women
Verbatim_Quote: Healing a broken heart is a popular reason why people travel alone. Others, like me, enjoy traveling alone because it is a pleasurable experience. It does not have to be sad!

Segment_ID: 25+ Solo Travel Safety Tips for Women _ Sojournies.html_P007
Source_Document: 25+ Solo Travel Safety Tips for Women _ Sojournies.html
Document_Title: 25+ Solo Travel Safety Tips for Women
Verbatim_Quote: Most solo travelers don’t admit it, but traveling solo is risky. You are going to a new country or city where you know no one. You don’t speak the language, have to learn new navigation, and aren’t familiar with customs. These safety tips can reduce risk, but there is no way to make solo travel 100% safe.

Segment_ID: 25+ Solo Travel Safety Tips for Women _ Sojournies.html_P008
Source_Document: 25+ Solo Travel Safety Tips for Women _ Sojournies.html
Document_Title: 25+ Solo Travel Safety Tips for Women
Verbatim_Quote: Safety tips for solo female travelers before you go

Segment_ID: 25+ Solo Travel Safety Tips for Women _ Sojournies.html_P009
Source_Document: 25+ Solo Travel Safety Tips for Women _ Sojournies.html
Document_Title: 25+ Solo Travel Safety Tips for Women
Verbatim_Quote: Understand your strengths and weaknesses

Segment_ID: 25+ Solo Travel Safety Tips for Women _ Sojournies.html_P010
Source_Document: 25+ Solo Travel Safety Tips for Women _ Sojournies.html
Document_Title: 25+ Solo Travel Safety Tips for Women
Verbatim_Quote: There can be a lot of solo travel anxiety before your solo trip! How do you navigate a new country? Are you a pro at eating alone? How well do you respond under pressure when no one you know is around? Are you open to meeting new people?

Segment_ID: 25+ Solo Travel Safety Tips for Women _ Sojournies.html_P011
Source_Document: 25+ Solo Travel Safety Tips for Women _ Sojournies.html
Document_Title: 25+ Solo Travel Safety Tips for Women
Verbatim_Quote: You should ask yourself these things when doing an inventory of your strengths and weaknesses. You never know what travel situations will arise on your trip. But knowing what you are, and are not good at, can help.

Segment_ID: 25+ Solo Travel Safety Tips for Women _ Sojournies.html_P012
Source_Document: 25+ Solo Travel Safety Tips for Women _ Sojournies.html
Document_Title: 25+ Solo Travel Safety Tips for Women
Verbatim_Quote: Read up on the location’s news

Segment_ID: 25+ Solo Travel Safety Tips for Women _ Sojournies.html_P013
Source_Document: 25+ Solo Travel Safety Tips for Women _ Sojournies.html
Document_Title: 25+ Solo Travel Safety Tips for Women
Verbatim_Quote: Watching the news is one of the underrated solo travel safety tips. At the same time, a lot of information scares people into not traveling to certain places. Knowing about the current political context of the site you’re visiting is good. Because if there is civil unrest, chances are your trip might be canceled or delayed, so you can prepare just in case.

Segment_ID: 25+ Solo Travel Safety Tips for Women _ Sojournies.html_P014
Source_Document: 25+ Solo Travel Safety Tips for Women _ Sojournies.html
Document_Title: 25+ Solo Travel Safety Tips for Women
Verbatim_Quote: Travel insurance is one of those things that people often think they will never need. But options such as World Nomads and Safety Wing are helpful to invest in. And you pay for travel insurance based on the number of days you travel.

Segment_ID: 25+ Solo Travel Safety Tips for Women _ Sojournies.html_P015
Source_Document: 25+ Solo Travel Safety Tips for Women _ Sojournies.html
Document_Title: 25+ Solo Travel Safety Tips for Women
Verbatim_Quote: Accidents happen while solo traveling, and sometimes a hospital is not nearby. But a travel first aid kit is handy because you have everything you need on the go. Be sure to buy one small enough not to take up too much space in your backpack or suitcase.

Segment_ID: 25+ Solo Travel Safety Tips for Women _ Sojournies.html_P016
Source_Document: 25+ Solo Travel Safety Tips for Women _ Sojournies.html
Document_Title: 25+ Solo Travel Safety Tips for Women
Verbatim_Quote: Add protecting your technology to your solo travel safety tips! Many people must realize that most Wi-Fi, airports, and other public places are insecure. However, with a VPN, such as Surfshark, you can protect your data or any information on your devices with a private network.

Segment_ID: 25+ Solo Travel Safety Tips for Women _ Sojournies.html_P017
Source_Document: 25+ Solo Travel Safety Tips for Women _ Sojournies.html
Document_Title: 25+ Solo Travel Safety Tips for Women
Verbatim_Quote: Something that most solo travelers don’t talk about is how expensive it is to travel by yourself. That’s why investing in a good travel credit card is critical. You can get points for your travel expenses, adding up to a free trip.

Segment_ID: 25+ Solo Travel Safety Tips for Women _ Sojournies.html_P018
Source_Document: 25+ Solo Travel Safety Tips for Women _ Sojournies.html
Document_Title: 25+ Solo Travel Safety Tips for Women
Verbatim_Quote: My favorite is the Chase Sapphire Preferred, which has a $95 annual fee. You can rack up many points when eating, taking rideshares like Lyft, and other travel expenses. I’ve had other cards, but this one is a solid choice.

Segment_ID: 25+ Solo Travel Safety Tips for Women _ Sojournies.html_P019
Source_Document: 25+ Solo Travel Safety Tips for Women _ Sojournies.html
Document_Title: 25+ Solo Travel Safety Tips for Women
Verbatim_Quote: Print copies of your documents

Segment_ID: 25+ Solo Travel Safety Tips for Women _ Sojournies.html_P020
Source_Document: 25+ Solo Travel Safety Tips for Women _ Sojournies.html
Document_Title: 25+ Solo Travel Safety Tips for Women
Verbatim_Quote: Making copies of your important documents should be at the top of your solo travel safety tips list. These include your passport and a visa if you need one to enter the country. You never know when an emergency can arise. And just in case your passport is stolen, having backups is beneficial.

Segment_ID: 25+ Solo Travel Safety Tips for Women _ Sojournies.html_P021
Source_Document: 25+ Solo Travel Safety Tips for Women _ Sojournies.html
Document_Title: 25+ Solo Travel Safety Tips for Women
Verbatim_Quote: Check your international data plan

Segment_ID: 25+ Solo Travel Safety Tips for Women _ Sojournies.html_P022
Source_Document: 25+ Solo Travel Safety Tips for Women _ Sojournies.html
Document_Title: 25+ Solo Travel Safety Tips for Women
Verbatim_Quote: We use our phones for everything these days, so having data at least is essential. So on your solo travel checklist, call your phone carrier to learn about your international data options. However, if those are too expensive, you can always get a local SIM card and the city/country you are visiting. You can also buy portable wi-fi like Travel Wifi!

Segment_ID: 25+ Solo Travel Safety Tips for Women _ Sojournies.html_P023
Source_Document: 25+ Solo Travel Safety Tips for Women _ Sojournies.html
Document_Title: 25+ Solo Travel Safety Tips for Women
Verbatim_Quote: Tell your bank you are leaving

Segment_ID: 25+ Solo Travel Safety Tips for Women _ Sojournies.html_P024
Source_Document: 25+ Solo Travel Safety Tips for Women _ Sojournies.html
Document_Title: 25+ Solo Travel Safety Tips for Women
Verbatim_Quote: Do not get your accounts closed! Before you head out for your solo trip, visit your bank. Let them know where you’ll be traveling and how long you’ll be gone so they can monitor for suspicious transactions. If not, they may cut off your cards, and you’ll have no money while on your solo trip.

Segment_ID: 25+ Solo Travel Safety Tips for Women _ Sojournies.html_P025
Source_Document: 25+ Solo Travel Safety Tips for Women _ Sojournies.html
Document_Title: 25+ Solo Travel Safety Tips for Women
Verbatim_Quote: How to be safe traveling alone as a woman

Segment_ID: 25+ Solo Travel Safety Tips for Women _ Sojournies.html_P026
Source_Document: 25+ Solo Travel Safety Tips for Women _ Sojournies.html
Document_Title: 25+ Solo Travel Safety Tips for Women
Verbatim_Quote: You never know what can happen while you are traveling solo. Put your itinerary in Google Docs or Padlet, and share it with friends and family back home. Since you are traveling where you don’t know anyone, it’s good for others to see where you are.

Segment_ID: 25+ Solo Travel Safety Tips for Women _ Sojournies.html_P027
Source_Document: 25+ Solo Travel Safety Tips for Women _ Sojournies.html
Document_Title: 25+ Solo Travel Safety Tips for Women
Verbatim_Quote: It is best to navigate a new place during the daytime! That’s when booking your flights try to avoid arriving at night. It may make you more anxious when you can’t see your surroundings. So an earlier flight can prevent that unnecessary anxiety.

Segment_ID: 25+ Solo Travel Safety Tips for Women _ Sojournies.html_P028
Source_Document: 25+ Solo Travel Safety Tips for Women _ Sojournies.html
Document_Title: 25+ Solo Travel Safety Tips for Women
Verbatim_Quote: Only carry some of your money with you while traveling solo. Always have some cash in your suitcase or another hidden spot in your room. In case you are robbed, you want to have some backup money.

Segment_ID: 25+ Solo Travel Safety Tips for Women _ Sojournies.html_P030
Source_Document: 25+ Solo Travel Safety Tips for Women _ Sojournies.html
Document_Title: 25+ Solo Travel Safety Tips for Women
Verbatim_Quote: Speaking of robberies, never use your back pockets. While this tip may sound like common sense, it still happens. For alternatives to using your back pockets, continue reading about the safety items you must purchase for your solo trip to learn about the belt bag.

Segment_ID: 25+ Solo Travel Safety Tips for Women _ Sojournies.html_P031
Source_Document: 25+ Solo Travel Safety Tips for Women _ Sojournies.html
Document_Title: 25+ Solo Travel Safety Tips for Women
Verbatim_Quote: Do not engage in reckless behavior

Segment_ID: 25+ Solo Travel Safety Tips for Women _ Sojournies.html_P032
Source_Document: 25+ Solo Travel Safety Tips for Women _ Sojournies.html
Document_Title: 25+ Solo Travel Safety Tips for Women
Verbatim_Quote: I am all for being delusional and pursuing new adventures while traveling. However, there is a difference between curious and reckless. You do not want to get arrested or in trouble in a foreign country. So avoid situations that are illegal or put you in too much danger.

Segment_ID: 25+ Solo Travel Safety Tips for Women _ Sojournies.html_P033
Source_Document: 25+ Solo Travel Safety Tips for Women _ Sojournies.html
Document_Title: 25+ Solo Travel Safety Tips for Women
Verbatim_Quote: No one expects solo travelers to be fluent in every language of every country they visit. But knowing a few keywords and phrases is one of many resourceful solo travel safety tips. And it’s a great way to get to know a small part of the local community you are visiting.

Segment_ID: 25+ Solo Travel Safety Tips for Women _ Sojournies.html_P034
Source_Document: 25+ Solo Travel Safety Tips for Women _ Sojournies.html
Document_Title: 25+ Solo Travel Safety Tips for Women
Verbatim_Quote: Do not tell everyone you are traveling solo

Segment_ID: 25+ Solo Travel Safety Tips for Women _ Sojournies.html_P035
Source_Document: 25+ Solo Travel Safety Tips for Women _ Sojournies.html
Document_Title: 25+ Solo Travel Safety Tips for Women
Verbatim_Quote: Of all the safety tips for solo female travelers, this is one rule I break often. If you trust your gut, there may be one or two people you tell that you are traveling alone. But do not scream it from the rooftops. Be open yet discreet.

Segment_ID: 25+ Solo Travel Safety Tips for Women _ Sojournies.html_P036
Source_Document: 25+ Solo Travel Safety Tips for Women _ Sojournies.html
Document_Title: 25+ Solo Travel Safety Tips for Women
Verbatim_Quote: Reading is fundamental. Whether you are booking a tour, transportation, or accommodations such as hostels, you need to read the reviews. They can tell you so much about other solo travelers’ experiences for you to make an informed decision about your trip.

Segment_ID: 25+ Solo Travel Safety Tips for Women _ Sojournies.html_P037
Source_Document: 25+ Solo Travel Safety Tips for Women _ Sojournies.html
Document_Title: 25+ Solo Travel Safety Tips for Women
Verbatim_Quote: Negotiate transportation costs beforehand

Segment_ID: 25+ Solo Travel Safety Tips for Women _ Sojournies.html_P038
Source_Document: 25+ Solo Travel Safety Tips for Women _ Sojournies.html
Document_Title: 25+ Solo Travel Safety Tips for Women
Verbatim_Quote: One of the biggest solo travel scams is being charged extra by taxis and other forms of transportation. Before you get in any vehicle, you need to negotiate the price before you go. Some drivers will try to charge extra for a ride.

Segment_ID: 25+ Solo Travel Safety Tips for Women _ Sojournies.html_P039
Source_Document: 25+ Solo Travel Safety Tips for Women _ Sojournies.html
Document_Title: 25+ Solo Travel Safety Tips for Women
Verbatim_Quote: While ATMs can be better for retrieving money than currency exchanges and airports, still be careful. Avoid ATMs and convenience stores, or third-party stations. I always take out cash at an ATM in the airport when I arrive. And when I’m in town, I go to a more crowded ATM in a public setting because they are less likely to be tampered with by robbers.

Segment_ID: 25+ Solo Travel Safety Tips for Women _ Sojournies.html_P040
Source_Document: 25+ Solo Travel Safety Tips for Women _ Sojournies.html
Document_Title: 25+ Solo Travel Safety Tips for Women
Verbatim_Quote: An alternative is to wait until you get settled in your accommodations, walk around, and see where the locals are retrieving cash. Those are less likely to be tourist traps. As a solo traveler, you should also look up local banks and see where their ATMs are, as they tend to be more reputable and reliable.

Segment_ID: 25+ Solo Travel Safety Tips for Women _ Sojournies.html_P041
Source_Document: 25+ Solo Travel Safety Tips for Women _ Sojournies.html
Document_Title: 25+ Solo Travel Safety Tips for Women
Verbatim_Quote: Best safety tips for traveling alone

Segment_ID: 25+ Solo Travel Safety Tips for Women _ Sojournies.html_P042
Source_Document: 25+ Solo Travel Safety Tips for Women _ Sojournies.html
Document_Title: 25+ Solo Travel Safety Tips for Women
Verbatim_Quote: Lying is one of the most unexpected but valuable safety tips for solo female travelers. When traveling in an Uber, say you are meeting with friends at your location. You can also mention that you have a fiancé if you get unwanted advances. But having a few key lies is helpful as an extra layer of protection for a solo traveler.

Segment_ID: 25+ Solo Travel Safety Tips for Women _ Sojournies.html_P043
Source_Document: 25+ Solo Travel Safety Tips for Women _ Sojournies.html
Document_Title: 25+ Solo Travel Safety Tips for Women
Verbatim_Quote: While in a rideshare, there are some ways to protect yourself. If you are using Uber, change your settings so that you give the driver a code once you get in. This is one of my favorite solo travel safety tips because it guarantees that you have the right Uber driver. They must put the code in first before they can drive off.

Segment_ID: 25+ Solo Travel Safety Tips for Women _ Sojournies.html_P044
Source_Document: 25+ Solo Travel Safety Tips for Women _ Sojournies.html
Document_Title: 25+ Solo Travel Safety Tips for Women
Verbatim_Quote: Fake it til you make it is the name of the game! Avoid looking down at your Google Maps when navigating to a tourist attraction, as it makes you look like a tourist. Try memorizing at least a few of the directions before you go. Confidence goes a long way; people will be less likely to target you.

Segment_ID: 25+ Solo Travel Safety Tips for Women _ Sojournies.html_P045
Source_Document: 25+ Solo Travel Safety Tips for Women _ Sojournies.html
Document_Title: 25+ Solo Travel Safety Tips for Women
Verbatim_Quote: Download the local transportation app

Segment_ID: 25+ Solo Travel Safety Tips for Women _ Sojournies.html_P046
Source_Document: 25+ Solo Travel Safety Tips for Women _ Sojournies.html
Document_Title: 25+ Solo Travel Safety Tips for Women
Verbatim_Quote: Uber is a common rideshare transportation app. Yet, some cities have apps to help you navigate that are better. When researching a town for a trip, be sure to check if there is a better option.

Segment_ID: 25+ Solo Travel Safety Tips for Women _ Sojournies.html_P047
Source_Document: 25+ Solo Travel Safety Tips for Women _ Sojournies.html
Document_Title: 25+ Solo Travel Safety Tips for Women
Verbatim_Quote: Top 5 safety devices for solo travelers

Segment_ID: 25+ Solo Travel Safety Tips for Women _ Sojournies.html_P048
Source_Document: 25+ Solo Travel Safety Tips for Women _ Sojournies.html
Document_Title: 25+ Solo Travel Safety Tips for Women
Verbatim_Quote: Of all the solo travel safety tips, this one is key for staying in hostels, hotels, and Airbnb. A door alarm or lock makes solo female travelers feel more secure in their accommodations. I recommend this one that slides under your door and this one that slides on the side. I carry both because every door is different.

Verbatim_Quote: Another critical safety item for solo female travelers is a safety alarm. Unlike the door alarms, this Birdie one you carry with you to create a distraction. The warning has a loud siren and strobe light that signals to others you are in trouble.

Verbatim_Quote: I recommend putting your essential documents in this bag when boarding any transportation during your trip. A belt bag is also suitable for smaller items when you are hiking. Just make sure you put the pocket in front of you so no one can pick your pocket.

Document_Title: 25+ Solo Travel Safety Tips for Women
Verbatim_Quote: This last tip is for solo travelers who will stay in hostels. You will need a lock if you decide to book a dorm instead of a private room. Solo female travelers store their backpacks and other belongings in a locker. But many need to bring a padlock lock to keep their stuff safe. Pack one TSA-safe with you so you can also use it on the plane.

Document_Title: 25+ Solo Travel Safety Tips for Women
Verbatim_Quote: Fear stops so many people from solo traveling. But you should channel that fear and travel scared anyway. There is something about challenging yourself and doing an experience out of your comfort zone that is exhilarating.

Segment_ID: 5 surprising things you learn as a solo female traveler - Young Adventuress.html_P001
Source_Document: 5 surprising things you learn as a solo female traveler - Young Adventuress.html
Document_Title: 5 surprising things you learn as a solo female traveler
Verbatim_Quote: Home » Blog » Adventures » 5 surprising things you learn as a solo female traveler

Segment_ID: 5 surprising things you learn as a solo female traveler - Young Adventuress.html_P002
Source_Document: 5 surprising things you learn as a solo female traveler - Young Adventuress.html
Document_Title: 5 surprising things you learn as a solo female traveler
Verbatim_Quote: How easy would life be if we could just agree on everything?

Segment_ID: 5 surprising things you learn as a solo female traveler - Young Adventuress.html_P003
Source_Document: 5 surprising things you learn as a solo female traveler - Young Adventuress.html
Document_Title: 5 surprising things you learn as a solo female traveler
Verbatim_Quote: But where’s the fun in that? I’ve got a lot of opinions about a lot of things, though I spent most of my life keeping my thoughts to myself. It wasn’t until I went away to college that I finally found confidence in expressing them. Maybe it’s been the same journey for you too.

Segment_ID: 5 surprising things you learn as a solo female traveler - Young Adventuress.html_P004
Source_Document: 5 surprising things you learn as a solo female traveler - Young Adventuress.html
Document_Title: 5 surprising things you learn as a solo female traveler
Verbatim_Quote: Where was I going with this? Ah yes, one of my big big BIG opinions that I frequently and loudly profess in real life as well as online is the following; I am a strong believer that all women should travel solo, at least once in their lives.

Segment_ID: 5 surprising things you learn as a solo female traveler - Young Adventuress.html_P005
Source_Document: 5 surprising things you learn as a solo female traveler - Young Adventuress.html
Document_Title: 5 surprising things you learn as a solo female traveler
Verbatim_Quote: Looking at that statement, on the surface it really doesn’t seem too bold or controversial, and yet sadly it’s filled with layers and layers of complications.

Segment_ID: 5 surprising things you learn as a solo female traveler - Young Adventuress.html_P006
Source_Document: 5 surprising things you learn as a solo female traveler - Young Adventuress.html
Document_Title: 5 surprising things you learn as a solo female traveler
Verbatim_Quote: It’s been ages since my Solo Female Traveler’s Manifesto and I thought it was high time to revisit a topic close to my heart.

Segment_ID: 5 surprising things you learn as a solo female traveler - Young Adventuress.html_P007
Source_Document: 5 surprising things you learn as a solo female traveler - Young Adventuress.html
Document_Title: 5 surprising things you learn as a solo female traveler
Verbatim_Quote: The sad truth is that many women chose not to travel alone, for one reason or anything – there is always a reason, or better put, an excuse. And I am not saying that all women should become perpetual solo travelers either; everyone has their own way of living and travel style, and I don’t know about you guys, but when people tell me what to do or how to live, I immediately do the opposite.

Segment_ID: 5 surprising things you learn as a solo female traveler - Young Adventuress.html_P008
Source_Document: 5 surprising things you learn as a solo female traveler - Young Adventuress.html
Document_Title: 5 surprising things you learn as a solo female traveler
Verbatim_Quote: This case is different; hear me out. I believe it’s up to you to decide when and where and how you travel. All of us are different and work and function (or like me, not function) in different ways. But I thought as I like to overshare as a general rule, I’d go ahead and talk about 5 things I’ve learned over the years as a perpetual solo female traveler and what it’s taught me about life. Cuz it’s a lot.

Segment_ID: 5 surprising things you learn as a solo female traveler - Young Adventuress.html_P009
Source_Document: 5 surprising things you learn as a solo female traveler - Young Adventuress.html
Document_Title: 5 surprising things you learn as a solo female traveler
Verbatim_Quote: 1. You find some independence, hopefully

Segment_ID: 5 surprising things you learn as a solo female traveler - Young Adventuress.html_P010
Source_Document: 5 surprising things you learn as a solo female traveler - Young Adventuress.html
Document_Title: 5 surprising things you learn as a solo female traveler
Verbatim_Quote: It’s not to say I wasn’t independent before I took my first trip alone, but until you have to organize and sort out everything on your own, make snap decisions on the road, stay on budget and basically take care of yourself without someone to lean on, you never are really independent, are you?

Segment_ID: 5 surprising things you learn as a solo female traveler - Young Adventuress.html_P011
Source_Document: 5 surprising things you learn as a solo female traveler - Young Adventuress.html
Document_Title: 5 surprising things you learn as a solo female traveler
Verbatim_Quote: This is probably going to get me hate mail, but I have met sooooo many girls over the years who are dependent, needy, first-class clingers who are basically incapable of getting around without a friend, family member or boyfriend in tow. I’m sure you’ve seen it. Girls who are incapable of being alone.

Segment_ID: 5 surprising things you learn as a solo female traveler - Young Adventuress.html_P012
Source_Document: 5 surprising things you learn as a solo female traveler - Young Adventuress.html
Document_Title: 5 surprising things you learn as a solo female traveler
Verbatim_Quote: Obviously I’ve met plenty of girls who are the opposite too, there’s a massive range, but the ones that stick in my mind are the ones who either blow me away with how strong they are, or the ones that I can’t really wrap my head around how they function day to day.

Segment_ID: 5 surprising things you learn as a solo female traveler - Young Adventuress.html_P013
Source_Document: 5 surprising things you learn as a solo female traveler - Young Adventuress.html
Document_Title: 5 surprising things you learn as a solo female traveler
Verbatim_Quote: Do we hear guys talking about the same problem? And usually when people worry about solo travelers, it’s geared towards women, like we can’t take care of ourselves. Ah Ben is going to travel South America for 3 months, good for him! But when Liz wants to go to Africa, oh no no no!

Segment_ID: 5 surprising things you learn as a solo female traveler - Young Adventuress.html_P014
Source_Document: 5 surprising things you learn as a solo female traveler - Young Adventuress.html
Document_Title: 5 surprising things you learn as a solo female traveler
Verbatim_Quote: I don’t know about you all, but I don’t want that stereotype to perpetuate any longer!

Segment_ID: 5 surprising things you learn as a solo female traveler - Young Adventuress.html_P015
Source_Document: 5 surprising things you learn as a solo female traveler - Young Adventuress.html
Document_Title: 5 surprising things you learn as a solo female traveler
Verbatim_Quote: I believe that every girl should hit the road at some point in their lives alone. No companions. Just roam.

Segment_ID: 5 surprising things you learn as a solo female traveler - Young Adventuress.html_P016
Source_Document: 5 surprising things you learn as a solo female traveler - Young Adventuress.html
Document_Title: 5 surprising things you learn as a solo female traveler
Verbatim_Quote: For me, all of those decisions, my independence is second-nature now. I don’t think twice about it. It doesn’t seem hard or challenging to me anymore. In fact, traveling in a group now is MORE difficult for me. Who would have ever thought?

Segment_ID: 5 surprising things you learn as a solo female traveler - Young Adventuress.html_P017
Source_Document: 5 surprising things you learn as a solo female traveler - Young Adventuress.html
Document_Title: 5 surprising things you learn as a solo female traveler
Verbatim_Quote: Solo travel taught me to grow up and that is only ever one person in the entire world you can always depend on – yourself.

Segment_ID: 5 surprising things you learn as a solo female traveler - Young Adventuress.html_P018
Source_Document: 5 surprising things you learn as a solo female traveler - Young Adventuress.html
Document_Title: 5 surprising things you learn as a solo female traveler
Verbatim_Quote: 2. You’ll grow some travel smarts and learn that you can trust people

Segment_ID: 5 surprising things you learn as a solo female traveler - Young Adventuress.html_P019
Source_Document: 5 surprising things you learn as a solo female traveler - Young Adventuress.html
Document_Title: 5 surprising things you learn as a solo female traveler
Verbatim_Quote: In my opinion one of the best things you learn traveling alone is intuition. Hear me out!

Segment_ID: 5 surprising things you learn as a solo female traveler - Young Adventuress.html_P020
Source_Document: 5 surprising things you learn as a solo female traveler - Young Adventuress.html
Document_Title: 5 surprising things you learn as a solo female traveler
Verbatim_Quote: In this day and age I think people like hard facts, not wishy-washy philosophical ideas. I feel like many people want to know exactly what they are going to get out of a trip, travel or experience abroad, and to hear someone reply with “intuition” isn’t exactly concrete.

Segment_ID: 5 surprising things you learn as a solo female traveler - Young Adventuress.html_P021
Source_Document: 5 surprising things you learn as a solo female traveler - Young Adventuress.html
Document_Title: 5 surprising things you learn as a solo female traveler
Verbatim_Quote: That being said, I stand by 100% in my statement that over time, traveling alone will give you certain instincts; likely you’ll learn to read people really well, understand the difference between someone being friendly and when it’s weird, and when you are ok, or when you should run like hell.

Segment_ID: 5 surprising things you learn as a solo female traveler - Young Adventuress.html_P022
Source_Document: 5 surprising things you learn as a solo female traveler - Young Adventuress.html
Document_Title: 5 surprising things you learn as a solo female traveler
Verbatim_Quote: I think a big reason why I never really have problems on the road is that I can read situations very, very well, and if I feel uncomfortable in any way, I’m out of there. Boom. Gone. I have some serious self-preservation skills and I have no intention of ending tied up in the back of someone’s van.

Segment_ID: 5 surprising things you learn as a solo female traveler - Young Adventuress.html_P023
Source_Document: 5 surprising things you learn as a solo female traveler - Young Adventuress.html
Document_Title: 5 surprising things you learn as a solo female traveler
Verbatim_Quote: That being said, one of my absolute favorite things about travel is meeting locals, and getting to know them and share experiences or beautiful moments on the road. I never want to compromise that. That means I’m moderately skeptical but still openminded when I meet locals traveling. I like trusting people, and I don’t want to lose that or become suspicious or bitter. I like being open.

Segment_ID: 5 surprising things you learn as a solo female traveler - Young Adventuress.html_P024
Source_Document: 5 surprising things you learn as a solo female traveler - Young Adventuress.html
Document_Title: 5 surprising things you learn as a solo female traveler
Verbatim_Quote: Cautious optimism and intuition comes with experience.

Segment_ID: 5 surprising things you learn as a solo female traveler - Young Adventuress.html_P025
Source_Document: 5 surprising things you learn as a solo female traveler - Young Adventuress.html
Document_Title: 5 surprising things you learn as a solo female traveler
Verbatim_Quote: I get a lot of questions about where first time solo travelers should head, and I tend to say stick to “easier” or “friendlier” places first and build from there. Obviously, that part is questionable and varies person to person, but in my opinion, it’s better to build up and gain experience with each place you visit. Like maybe try Iceland before Egypt or New Zealand before Russia. But honestly, it doesn’t really matter. Sink or swim, you’ll learn either way.

Segment_ID: 5 surprising things you learn as a solo female traveler - Young Adventuress.html_P027
Source_Document: 5 surprising things you learn as a solo female traveler - Young Adventuress.html
Document_Title: 5 surprising things you learn as a solo female traveler
Verbatim_Quote: 3. You’ll learn that the world isn’t actually that dangerous

Segment_ID: 5 surprising things you learn as a solo female traveler - Young Adventuress.html_P028
Source_Document: 5 surprising things you learn as a solo female traveler - Young Adventuress.html
Document_Title: 5 surprising things you learn as a solo female traveler
Verbatim_Quote: I love this – the world isn’t as dangerous as we are told all the freaking time. News. Social media. Our families. We live in a world filled with negative stereotypes, generalizations, phobias and fears, and I fucking hate it. I hate it!

Segment_ID: 5 surprising things you learn as a solo female traveler - Young Adventuress.html_P029
Source_Document: 5 surprising things you learn as a solo female traveler - Young Adventuress.html
Document_Title: 5 surprising things you learn as a solo female traveler
Verbatim_Quote: If there is one lesson I value above all others from my experiences traveling, it’s that it’s taught me to ignore all of the negativity (within reason) and realize that people are people, no matter what color their skin is, what their religion is, or where they are from. Of course, there are bad people everywhere and shit does happen, but in comparison to all the beautiful souls out there and all the amazing, positive happy things you experience traveling, the good outweighs the bad.

Segment_ID: 5 surprising things you learn as a solo female traveler - Young Adventuress.html_P030
Source_Document: 5 surprising things you learn as a solo female traveler - Young Adventuress.html
Document_Title: 5 surprising things you learn as a solo female traveler
Verbatim_Quote: Violence against women is an international problem, and I don’t really see how it’s related to travel. Look at all these women getting raped in the US and the rapists go unpunished. Are we really a nation to be tossing judgements around about safety for women overseas?

Segment_ID: 5 surprising things you learn as a solo female traveler - Young Adventuress.html_P031
Source_Document: 5 surprising things you learn as a solo female traveler - Young Adventuress.html
Document_Title: 5 surprising things you learn as a solo female traveler
Verbatim_Quote: Terrible things can happen at home and overseas; what does travel have to do with it? Are we really in MORE danger in a foreign place?

Segment_ID: 5 surprising things you learn as a solo female traveler - Young Adventuress.html_P032
Source_Document: 5 surprising things you learn as a solo female traveler - Young Adventuress.html
Document_Title: 5 surprising things you learn as a solo female traveler
Verbatim_Quote: I wish more people would tell me good job for getting out and seeing the world on my own than warning me against it. Especially from people who travel less than I do. Um, I think I *might* know better about my own safety, thankyouverymuch.

Segment_ID: 5 surprising things you learn as a solo female traveler - Young Adventuress.html_P033
Source_Document: 5 surprising things you learn as a solo female traveler - Young Adventuress.html
Document_Title: 5 surprising things you learn as a solo female traveler
Verbatim_Quote: The only time I have ever felt truly threatened and afraid was on the metro in Washington D.C. where I grew up. Not Turkey. Not Egypt. Not Spain. Not Mongolia, and definitely not New Zealand or the 40 other countries I have been to. I wish people would remember that.

Segment_ID: 5 surprising things you learn as a solo female traveler - Young Adventuress.html_P034
Source_Document: 5 surprising things you learn as a solo female traveler - Young Adventuress.html
Document_Title: 5 surprising things you learn as a solo female traveler
Verbatim_Quote: On a side-note, while I believe the world is actually a lot safer than we are led to believe, accidents do still happen on the road, often when we are least expecting them! Which is why it’s so important to have a suitable travel insurance plan in place. I use World Nomads Travel Insurance, who I 100% recommend. Their policies are customizable, affordable AND include almost every adventure sport you can think of!

Segment_ID: 5 surprising things you learn as a solo female traveler - Young Adventuress.html_P035
Source_Document: 5 surprising things you learn as a solo female traveler - Young Adventuress.html
Document_Title: 5 surprising things you learn as a solo female traveler
Verbatim_Quote: 4. Relating to anyone is a skill you’ll pick up if you’re openminded

Segment_ID: 5 surprising things you learn as a solo female traveler - Young Adventuress.html_P036
Source_Document: 5 surprising things you learn as a solo female traveler - Young Adventuress.html
Document_Title: 5 surprising things you learn as a solo female traveler
Verbatim_Quote: I started traveling alone when I was 19. When I look back on the person who I was and the person I am today, I couldn’t be happier. I can’t wait to see how I turn out when I’m 80. I am a big believer in the transformative power of travel, and I love that experiences overseas and around the world can help shape and mold you, even make you into a better person if you let them, you know, in a non-hippie kind of way.

Segment_ID: 5 surprising things you learn as a solo female traveler - Young Adventuress.html_P037
Source_Document: 5 surprising things you learn as a solo female traveler - Young Adventuress.html
Document_Title: 5 surprising things you learn as a solo female traveler
Verbatim_Quote: Perhaps the most important skill I’ve picked up from solo traveling, at least the most important to me personally, is learning to be able to relate to anyone I meet on the road. Seriously, anyone.

Segment_ID: 5 surprising things you learn as a solo female traveler - Young Adventuress.html_P038
Source_Document: 5 surprising things you learn as a solo female traveler - Young Adventuress.html
Document_Title: 5 surprising things you learn as a solo female traveler
Verbatim_Quote: As much as I am an introvert at heart, I love talking to strangers and meeting people on the road. Without any companions or friends to lean on, I had to learn this on my own.

Segment_ID: 5 surprising things you learn as a solo female traveler - Young Adventuress.html_P039
Source_Document: 5 surprising things you learn as a solo female traveler - Young Adventuress.html
Document_Title: 5 surprising things you learn as a solo female traveler
Verbatim_Quote: I’ve made it a point in all my years of travel to be openminded, especially around people I don’t necessarily agree with or even like. Whether it’s a camel driver in the deserts of Jordan or shopkeeper in Indonesia, a sheep farmer in New Zealand or even an eagle hunter in Mongolia, people of all walks of life who couldn’t live or be any different from me, I still want to be able to sit down and talk to them, pick their brains, share stories and maybe even have a moment.

Segment_ID: 5 surprising things you learn as a solo female traveler - Young Adventuress.html_P040
Source_Document: 5 surprising things you learn as a solo female traveler - Young Adventuress.html
Document_Title: 5 surprising things you learn as a solo female traveler
Verbatim_Quote: My biggest fear is coming off as a cold, disinterested foreigner who doesn’t give a shit or makes no effort. I can’t stand that attitude among travelers, and trust me, I see it a lot.

Segment_ID: 5 surprising things you learn as a solo female traveler - Young Adventuress.html_P041
Source_Document: 5 surprising things you learn as a solo female traveler - Young Adventuress.html
Document_Title: 5 surprising things you learn as a solo female traveler
Verbatim_Quote: I’ve found that as a solo female traveler, people are MORE open with me and more welcoming. I suppose I am not very intimidating, and oftentimes I hear the whole “oh you crazy” for going around the world on my own, so I think people often take a protective, almost motherly attitude towards me, which is fine by me! Especially when I get fed.

Segment_ID: 5 surprising things you learn as a solo female traveler - Young Adventuress.html_P042
Source_Document: 5 surprising things you learn as a solo female traveler - Young Adventuress.html
Document_Title: 5 surprising things you learn as a solo female traveler
Verbatim_Quote: Those are the best things that happen on the road, at least for me, because they mean something.

Segment_ID: 5 surprising things you learn as a solo female traveler - Young Adventuress.html_P043
Source_Document: 5 surprising things you learn as a solo female traveler - Young Adventuress.html
Document_Title: 5 surprising things you learn as a solo female traveler
Verbatim_Quote: It’s one thing to take a pretty picture and have some adventures while traveling, but it’s a whole other ball game when it changes your life or can lead to glimpses of a total foreign culture that you can begin to wrap your head around.

Segment_ID: 5 surprising things you learn as a solo female traveler - Young Adventuress.html_P044
Source_Document: 5 surprising things you learn as a solo female traveler - Young Adventuress.html
Document_Title: 5 surprising things you learn as a solo female traveler
Verbatim_Quote: Relating to people from around the world is the first step to building empathy, something I think is really important for travelers and people in general to have.

Segment_ID: 5 surprising things you learn as a solo female traveler - Young Adventuress.html_P045
Source_Document: 5 surprising things you learn as a solo female traveler - Young Adventuress.html
Document_Title: 5 surprising things you learn as a solo female traveler
Verbatim_Quote: Why does this person act the way they do? What motivates them? How is their culture different than mine and maybe even how is it the same? And then the hard stuff. This person is wearing all of the clothes they own. This kid doesn’t have shoes. That girl’s family died of a preventable disease in the US. That boy has never used a computer.

Segment_ID: 5 surprising things you learn as a solo female traveler - Young Adventuress.html_P046
Source_Document: 5 surprising things you learn as a solo female traveler - Young Adventuress.html
Document_Title: 5 surprising things you learn as a solo female traveler
Verbatim_Quote: Being able to be empathetic and relate to someone so different than you is one of the best things you can learn while traveling. It’ll open your heart and your mind and allow you to really experience another country or culture.

Segment_ID: 5 surprising things you learn as a solo female traveler - Young Adventuress.html_P047
Source_Document: 5 surprising things you learn as a solo female traveler - Young Adventuress.html

Document_Title: A Beginner's Guide to Safety: Solo Travel for Women
Verbatim_Quote: The world is a vast and wondrous place, brimming with untold adventures and experiences waiting to be discovered. For women, the allure of solo travel holds a particular magic, a chance to break free from routine, embrace independence, and explore the globe on their own terms. The idea of setting off on a solo journey can be both exhilarating and a little intimidating. It’s a leap of faith, a step into the unknown, and a testament to your courage and self-reliance.

Segment_ID: A Beginner's Guide to Safety_ Solo Travel for Women _ Blog - JustWravel.html_P002
Source_Document: A Beginner's Guide to Safety_ Solo Travel for Women _ Blog - JustWravel.html
Document_Title: A Beginner's Guide to Safety: Solo Travel for Women
Verbatim_Quote: This guide on safety tips for solo female travelers is designed to empower you, the modern woman, with the knowledge and confidence to embark on your own solo travel adventures. We’ll cover everything from meticulous planning and practical packing tips to essential safety measures and strategies for making the most of your journey. This isn’t just about seeing the world; it’s about discovering yourself, pushing your boundaries, and returning home with a renewed sense of confidence and independence.

Source_Document: A Beginner's Guide to Safety_ Solo Travel for Women _ Blog - JustWravel.html
Document_Title: A Beginner's Guide to Safety: Solo Travel for Women
Verbatim_Quote: So, whether you’re a seasoned YOLO kinda girl, starting to consider your first solo trip, or planning a trip with your girl gang, we hope this guide will inspire you, inform you, and give you the confidence to take the leap. The world is waiting to be explored, and you are ready to explore it. Get ready for an adventure that will change your life.

Segment_ID: A Beginner's Guide to Safety_ Solo Travel for Women _ Blog - JustWravel.html_P005
Source_Document: A Beginner's Guide to Safety_ Solo Travel for Women _ Blog - JustWravel.html
Document_Title: A Beginner's Guide to Safety: Solo Travel for Women
Verbatim_Quote: Choose your destination: Planning your solo trip is like laying the foundation for an incredible adventure. It’s where the magic begins, and the more thorough you are, the smoother your journey will be. First, decide where you want to go.

Segment_ID: A Beginner's Guide to Safety_ Solo Travel for Women _ Blog - JustWravel.html_P006
Source_Document: A Beginner's Guide to Safety_ Solo Travel for Women _ Blog - JustWravel.html
Document_Title: A Beginner's Guide to Safety: Solo Travel for Women
Verbatim_Quote: Set a budget: Next, set a realistic budget. This is crucial for avoiding financial stress during your trip. Factor in everything: flights, accommodation, food, activities, transportation, visas, and even souvenirs. Don’t forget to include a buffer for unexpected expenses.

Segment_ID: A Beginner's Guide to Safety_ Solo Travel for Women _ Blog - JustWravel.html_P007
Source_Document: A Beginner's Guide to Safety_ Solo Travel for Women _ Blog - JustWravel.html
Document_Title: A Beginner's Guide to Safety: Solo Travel for Women
Verbatim_Quote: Book flights and accommodation: Booking flights and accommodation in advance is generally recommended, especially if you’re traveling during peak season or to popular destinations. This not only secures your spot but often helps you snag better deals.

Segment_ID: A Beginner's Guide to Safety_ Solo Travel for Women _ Blog - JustWravel.html_P008
Source_Document: A Beginner's Guide to Safety_ Solo Travel for Women _ Blog - JustWravel.html
Document_Title: A Beginner's Guide to Safety: Solo Travel for Women
Verbatim_Quote: Research your destination: Research is your best friend during the planning phase. Learn about the local culture, customs, and laws. Understanding the local etiquette will help you navigate unfamiliar situations with grace and respect. Also, research the safety situation in your chosen destination.

Segment_ID: A Beginner's Guide to Safety_ Solo Travel for Women _ Blog - JustWravel.html_P009
Source_Document: A Beginner's Guide to Safety_ Solo Travel for Women _ Blog - JustWravel.html
Document_Title: A Beginner's Guide to Safety: Solo Travel for Women
Verbatim_Quote: Plan your itinerary: Finally, create a rough itinerary. This doesn’t have to be a rigid schedule, but it helps to have a general idea of what you want to see and do. This will help you make the most of your time and ensure you don’t miss out on any must-see attractions.

Segment_ID: A Beginner's Guide to Safety_ Solo Travel for Women _ Blog - JustWravel.html_P010
Source_Document: A Beginner's Guide to Safety_ Solo Travel for Women _ Blog - JustWravel.html
Document_Title: A Beginner's Guide to Safety: Solo Travel for Women
Verbatim_Quote: However, don’t over-plan! Leave room for spontaneity and unexpected detours. Some of the best travel experiences come from unplanned moments. Simply, follow these safety tips for solo female travelers.

Source_Document: A Beginner's Guide to Safety_ Solo Travel for Women _ Blog - JustWravel.html
Document_Title: A Beginner's Guide to Safety: Solo Travel for Women
Verbatim_Quote: Safety is non-negotiable for any traveler, but it’s especially crucial for women exploring the world solo. Being proactive and informed can significantly reduce risks and empower you to enjoy your adventure with confidence. Here’s a breakdown of essential safety tips:

Segment_ID: A Beginner's Guide to Safety_ Solo Travel for Women _ Blog - JustWravel.html_P013
Source_Document: A Beginner's Guide to Safety_ Solo Travel for Women _ Blog - JustWravel.html
Document_Title: A Beginner's Guide to Safety: Solo Travel for Women
Verbatim_Quote: Share your itinerary: Provide a detailed itinerary to a trusted friend or family member. Include flight details, accommodation addresses, planned activities, and expected check-in/check-out dates. If you deviate from your plan, inform them immediately.

Segment_ID: A Beginner's Guide to Safety_ Solo Travel for Women _ Blog - JustWravel.html_P014
Source_Document: A Beginner's Guide to Safety_ Solo Travel for Women _ Blog - JustWravel.html
Document_Title: A Beginner's Guide to Safety: Solo Travel for Women
Verbatim_Quote: Research your destination: Thoroughly research your destination’s safety profile. Are there specific areas to avoid? What are the common scams targeting tourists? Understanding local laws and customs is vital. Look up emergency contact numbers and the location of the nearest embassy or consulate.

Segment_ID: A Beginner's Guide to Safety_ Solo Travel for Women _ Blog - JustWravel.html_P015
Source_Document: A Beginner's Guide to Safety_ Solo Travel for Women _ Blog - JustWravel.html
Document_Title: A Beginner's Guide to Safety: Solo Travel for Women
Matched_Indicators: uncomfortable, situational awareness, trust your gut, instinct
Verbatim_Quote: Situational awareness is key: Be aware of your surroundings at all times. Trust your gut instinct. If a situation feels uncomfortable or unsafe, remove yourself immediately. Pay attention to local news and any safety advisories.

Segment_ID: A Beginner's Guide to Safety_ Solo Travel for Women _ Blog - JustWravel.html_P016
Source_Document: A Beginner's Guide to Safety_ Solo Travel for Women _ Blog - JustWravel.html
Document_Title: A Beginner's Guide to Safety: Solo Travel for Women
Matched_Indicators: walking alone at night, deserted, public space
Verbatim_Quote: Stay in well-lit and populated areas: Avoid walking alone at night, especially in poorly lit or deserted areas. Stick to well-trafficked streets and public spaces. If you must walk at night, consider traveling with a group or using a reputable ride-hailing app.

Segment_ID: A Beginner's Guide to Safety_ Solo Travel for Women _ Blog - JustWravel.html_P017
Source_Document: A Beginner's Guide to Safety_ Solo Travel for Women _ Blog - JustWravel.html
Document_Title: A Beginner's Guide to Safety: Solo Travel for Women
Verbatim_Quote: Be selective about sharing information: Be cautious about who you talk to and what personal information you share. Avoid discussing your travel plans or revealing where you’re staying with strangers.

Segment_ID: A Beginner's Guide to Safety_ Solo Travel for Women _ Blog - JustWravel.html_P018
Source_Document: A Beginner's Guide to Safety_ Solo Travel for Women _ Blog - JustWravel.html
Document_Title: A Beginner's Guide to Safety: Solo Travel for Women
Verbatim_Quote: Secure your valuables: Use a money belt, hidden pouch, or secure travel wallet to keep your cash, cards, and passport safe. Avoid displaying expensive jewelry, electronics, or large amounts of cash.

Segment_ID: A Beginner's Guide to Safety_ Solo Travel for Women _ Blog - JustWravel.html_P019
Source_Document: A Beginner's Guide to Safety_ Solo Travel for Women _ Blog - JustWravel.html
Document_Title: A Beginner's Guide to Safety: Solo Travel for Women
Verbatim_Quote: Stay connected (but be smart): While it’s important to stay connected with friends and family, be mindful of what you share on social media. Avoid posting real-time updates about your location, as this can make you a target for unwanted attention.

Segment_ID: A Beginner's Guide to Safety_ Solo Travel for Women _ Blog - JustWravel.html_P020
Source_Document: A Beginner's Guide to Safety_ Solo Travel for Women _ Blog - JustWravel.html
Document_Title: A Beginner's Guide to Safety: Solo Travel for Women
Verbatim_Quote: Transportation safety: When using taxis or ride-hailing apps, especially at night, verify the driver’s identity and license plate. Share your ride details with a friend or family member. Be wary of unmarked taxis or drivers who approach you unsolicited.

Segment_ID: A Beginner's Guide to Safety_ Solo Travel for Women _ Blog - JustWravel.html_P021
Source_Document: A Beginner's Guide to Safety_ Solo Travel for Women _ Blog - JustWravel.html
Document_Title: A Beginner's Guide to Safety: Solo Travel for Women
Verbatim_Quote: Food & Accommodation safety: Choose reputable accommodations with good security measures. Be cautious about accepting drinks from strangers. Never leave your drink unattended, and don’t accept drinks from someone you don’t trust.

Segment_ID: A Beginner's Guide to Safety_ Solo Travel for Women _ Blog - JustWravel.html_P022
Source_Document: A Beginner's Guide to Safety_ Solo Travel for Women _ Blog - JustWravel.html
Document_Title: A Beginner's Guide to Safety: Solo Travel for Women
Verbatim_Quote: Asking for help: Remember that it’s okay to ask for help. If you need help, approach families, couples, or women traveling alone. They are generally more likely to offer genuine assistance. Avoid approaching lone men, especially in isolated areas.

Segment_ID: A Beginner's Guide to Safety_ Solo Travel for Women _ Blog - JustWravel.html_P023
Source_Document: A Beginner's Guide to Safety_ Solo Travel for Women _ Blog - JustWravel.html
Document_Title: A Beginner's Guide to Safety: Solo Travel for Women
Verbatim_Quote: Blending in (when appropriate): While you should never compromise your safety, try to blend in with the local culture and avoid drawing unnecessary attention to yourself. Dress modestly and respectfully, and observe local customs and traditions. Knowing a few basic phrases in the local language can be helpful in emergencies and shows respect for the local culture.

Segment_ID: A Beginner's Guide to Safety_ Solo Travel for Women _ Blog - JustWravel.html_P024
Source_Document: A Beginner's Guide to Safety_ Solo Travel for Women _ Blog - JustWravel.html
Document_Title: A Beginner's Guide to Safety: Solo Travel for Women
Verbatim_Quote: Trust your instincts: Your intuition is a powerful tool. If a situation feels off or makes you uncomfortable, trust your gut and remove yourself from the situation. Don’t hesitate to seek help from local authorities or other trusted individuals.

Segment_ID: A Beginner's Guide to Safety_ Solo Travel for Women _ Blog - JustWravel.html_P025
Source_Document: A Beginner's Guide to Safety_ Solo Travel for Women _ Blog - JustWravel.html
Document_Title: A Beginner's Guide to Safety: Solo Travel for Women
Verbatim_Quote: Safety Items for Solo Female Travelers

Segment_ID: A Beginner's Guide to Safety_ Solo Travel for Women _ Blog - JustWravel.html_P026
Source_Document: A Beginner's Guide to Safety_ Solo Travel for Women _ Blog - JustWravel.html
Document_Title: A Beginner's Guide to Safety: Solo Travel for Women
Verbatim_Quote: Traveling alone as a woman requires careful planning, and a crucial aspect of that is prioritizing your safety. Apart from following all the safety tips for solo female travelers; carrying the right safety items can provide peace of mind and empower you to navigate unfamiliar situations with greater confidence. Here’s a look at some essential safety items for solo female travelers.

Segment_ID: A Beginner's Guide to Safety_ Solo Travel for Women _ Blog - JustWravel.html_P027
Source_Document: A Beginner's Guide to Safety_ Solo Travel for Women _ Blog - JustWravel.html
Document_Title: A Beginner's Guide to Safety: Solo Travel for Women
Verbatim_Quote: Personal Safety Alarm: This small, handheld device emits a piercingly loud siren (typically 120-130 decibels) when activated. The sudden noise can startle an attacker, disorient them, and attract attention. Test your alarm regularly to ensure it functions correctly. Some models include a built-in LED light, adding another layer of visibility.

Segment_ID: A Beginner's Guide to Safety_ Solo Travel for Women _ Blog - JustWravel.html_P028
Source_Document: A Beginner's Guide to Safety_ Solo Travel for Women _ Blog - JustWravel.html
Document_Title: A Beginner's Guide to Safety: Solo Travel for Women
Verbatim_Quote: Pepper Spray: A non-lethal self-defense spray containing an irritant that causes temporary burning and discomfort to the eyes, nose, and throat. It can incapacitate an attacker, giving you time to escape. Crucially, know how to use it. Seek self-defense training that includes pepper spray practice. Remember, it’s for self-defense only. Be aware of local laws regarding pepper spray, as it may be restricted or illegal in some areas. Less-lethal alternatives, such as bear spray (intended for bears but usable in extreme human encounters), may also be considered.

Segment_ID: A Beginner's Guide to Safety_ Solo Travel for Women _ Blog - JustWravel.html_P029
Source_Document: A Beginner's Guide to Safety_ Solo Travel for Women _ Blog - JustWravel.html
Document_Title: A Beginner's Guide to Safety: Solo Travel for Women
Verbatim_Quote: LED Rechargeable Flashlight: A bright flashlight is a multi-purpose tool. It can illuminate dark areas, signal for help, and even be used defensively by shining it in an attacker’s eyes. A tactical flashlight with a strobe function is even more effective. The rapidly flashing light can disorient and temporarily blind an attacker, giving you time to escape. Rechargeable models are best for travel, so you don’t have to worry about running out of batteries.

Segment_ID: A Beginner's Guide to Safety_ Solo Travel for Women _ Blog - JustWravel.html_P030
Source_Document: A Beginner's Guide to Safety_ Solo Travel for Women _ Blog - JustWravel.html
Document_Title: A Beginner's Guide to Safety: Solo Travel for Women
Verbatim_Quote: Padlock or Luggage Lock: A good lock can deter opportunistic theft. TSA-approved locks are essential for air travel. These locks allow airport security to inspect your luggage without cutting the lock, preventing damage to your belongings. While a lock won’t stop a determined thief, it can make your luggage a less appealing target.

Segment_ID: A Beginner's Guide to Safety_ Solo Travel for Women _ Blog - JustWravel.html_P031
Source_Document: A Beginner's Guide to Safety_ Solo Travel for Women _ Blog - JustWravel.html
Document_Title: A Beginner's Guide to Safety: Solo Travel for Women
Verbatim_Quote: Fanny Pack/Cross-body Bag: Keeping your valuables close to your body is crucial for preventing pickpocketing. A money belt worn discreetly under clothing is the most secure option. A cross-body bag worn in front is also a good choice. Avoid traditional fanny packs worn around the waist, as they can be easily targeted by thieves.

Segment_ID: A Beginner's Guide to Safety_ Solo Travel for Women _ Blog - JustWravel.html_P032
Source_Document: A Beginner's Guide to Safety_ Solo Travel for Women _ Blog - JustWravel.html
Document_Title: A Beginner's Guide to Safety: Solo Travel for Women
Verbatim_Quote: Copies of Important Documents: Losing your passport or other important documents can be a nightmare. Make digital copies of your passport, visa, driver’s license, travel insurance, and other essential documents. Store these copies securely in the cloud (using a password-protected service) or on a password-protected USB drive. Also, leave a copy of your itinerary with a trusted friend or family member.

Segment_ID: A Beginner's Guide to Safety_ Solo Travel for Women _ Blog - JustWravel.html_P033
Source_Document: A Beginner's Guide to Safety_ Solo Travel for Women _ Blog - JustWravel.html
Document_Title: A Beginner's Guide to Safety: Solo Travel for Women
Verbatim_Quote: Emergency Contact Information: Have a list of emergency contact numbers readily accessible. This should include local police, the nearest embassy or consulate, your family members, and your travel insurance provider. Program ICE (In Case of Emergency) contacts into your phone. This allows first responders to quickly access your emergency contacts even if your phone is locked.

Segment_ID: A Beginner's Guide to Safety_ Solo Travel for Women _ Blog - JustWravel.html_P034
Source_Document: A Beginner's Guide to Safety_ Solo Travel for Women _ Blog - JustWravel.html
Document_Title: A Beginner's Guide to Safety: Solo Travel for Women
Verbatim_Quote: First-Aid Kit: A small, well-stocked first-aid kit is essential for treating minor injuries and ailments. Include bandages, antiseptic wipes, pain relievers, any personal medications you need, and a small first-aid manual or app on your phone. Customize the kit to your specific needs. If you have allergies or medical conditions, make sure you have the necessary medications and supplies.

Segment_ID: A Beginner's Guide to Safety_ Solo Travel for Women _ Blog - JustWravel.html_P035
Source_Document: A Beginner's Guide to Safety_ Solo Travel for Women _ Blog - JustWravel.html
Document_Title: A Beginner's Guide to Safety: Solo Travel for Women
Verbatim_Quote: Portable Power Bank: Keeping your phone charged is critical, especially in an emergency. A portable power bank allows you to recharge your phone on the go. Choose a power bank with sufficient capacity to charge your phone multiple times.

Segment_ID: A Beginner's Guide to Safety_ Solo Travel for Women _ Blog - JustWravel.html_P036
Source_Document: A Beginner's Guide to Safety_ Solo Travel for Women _ Blog - JustWravel.html
Document_Title: A Beginner's Guide to Safety: Solo Travel for Women

Source_Document: A Beginner's Guide to Safety_ Solo Travel for Women _ Blog - JustWravel.html
Document_Title: A Beginner's Guide to Safety: Solo Travel for Women
Verbatim_Quote: Whistle: A loud, high-pitched whistle can be used to attract attention in an emergency. It’s a simple but effective tool.

Segment_ID: A Beginner's Guide to Safety_ Solo Travel for Women _ Blog - JustWravel.html_P038
Source_Document: A Beginner's Guide to Safety_ Solo Travel for Women _ Blog - JustWravel.html
Document_Title: A Beginner's Guide to Safety: Solo Travel for Women
Verbatim_Quote: Travel Insurance: Travel insurance is absolutely essential. It can protect you from financial losses due to medical emergencies, lost luggage, trip cancellations, and other unforeseen events. Make sure you have adequate coverage for your trip.

Segment_ID: A Beginner's Guide to Safety_ Solo Travel for Women _ Blog - JustWravel.html_P039
Source_Document: A Beginner's Guide to Safety_ Solo Travel for Women _ Blog - JustWravel.html
Document_Title: A Beginner's Guide to Safety: Solo Travel for Women
Verbatim_Quote: Local Laws and Customs: Before you travel, research the local laws and customs of your destination. This is especially important regarding self-defense tools. What’s legal in one country may be illegal in another. Understanding local customs can also help you avoid misunderstandings and potentially dangerous situations.

Segment_ID: A Beginner's Guide to Safety_ Solo Travel for Women _ Blog - JustWravel.html_P040
Source_Document: A Beginner's Guide to Safety_ Solo Travel for Women _ Blog - JustWravel.html
Document_Title: A Beginner's Guide to Safety: Solo Travel for Women
Verbatim_Quote: Remember, these safety items are tools to help you stay safe. The most important safety measure is to be aware of your surroundings, trust your instincts, and make smart choices. Combine these tools with good judgment and proactive planning for a safer and more enjoyable travel experience.

Segment_ID: A Beginner's Guide to Safety_ Solo Travel for Women _ Blog - JustWravel.html_P041
Source_Document: A Beginner's Guide to Safety_ Solo Travel for Women _ Blog - JustWravel.html
